title: SLO telemetry gating and proactive on-call suppression
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Our current SLO alerting is noisy for multi-tenant customers during transient infra events. Pager fatigue has increased on-call churn and the incident signal-to-noise ratio has fallen. Existing burn-rate alerts trigger broadly and don't account for tenant-level noise signatures or short-lived load spikes tied to background jobs or synthetic probes.

Goal: Implement a telemetry gating layer and a proactive on-call suppression policy that reduces false-positive paging while preserving true-positive SLO detection and maintaining total alert coverage. The system should: 1) learn lightweight tenant anomaly signatures from traces/metrics to suppress churny signals, 2) apply short-window gating rules (probabilistic and deterministic) before escalating to burn-rate paging, and 3) provide observability and auditability for suppressed alerts so PMs/support can review suppressed incidents.

Scope: Backend services to compute tenant signatures, a gating API in the alerting pipeline, instrumentation hooks in tracing ingest to attach signature tags, console UI to expose suppression decisions and audit logs, and a rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Telemetry gating service returns a suppression decision within 75ms p50 for 95% of API calls.
2) Production canary reduces pager volume for the selected tenants by >=30% without missing SLO breaches (validated by blind replay).
3) Suppressed alerts appear in the new 'Suppression Audit' dashboard with full context and can be re-opened manually.
4) No end-to-end SLO regression in latency/error SLOs during canary windows.
5) Team runbook updated with suppression tuning knobs and rollback steps.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: introduce a lightweight 'gating' microservice that consumes consolidated signals (burn-rate deltas, error spikes, trace-fingerprint matches) and outputs a deterministic/probabilistic 'suppress | escalate' decision.

Signature model: start with a deterministic signature (fingerprint) built from a small set of stable attributes: tenant_id, predominant error codes, top 3 slow path spans, and predominant user-agent patterns. Fingerprints are stored in a TTL cache and scored by recent occurrence frequency.

Fallbacks: If the gating service is unavailable, pipeline must default to escalate (fail-open) for critical SLOs and to safe-escalate (escalate with lower priority) for internal SLOs.

Data pipeline: add enrichment hook to span ingester to tag spans with tenant_fingerprint id. Use a short-lived materialized view to compute per-tenant spike rates and feed gating decisions.

Telemetry: expose metrics: gating_latencies, suppression_rate_by_tenant, suppressed_alert_reasons, false_suppression_incidents. Add tracing for gating decisions for audit.

Rollout: start with 5 low-risk tenants, monitor for 72h, expand with exponential ramp if no regressions.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: False suppression of real incidents. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, fail-open on unknown patterns, blind-replay test harness before go-live, and a permanent retention of suppressed alerts for immediate re-raise.
Risk: Added latency in alert path. Mitigation: keep gating p50 <75ms, cache decisions for short windows (30s), and add local in-memory fallbacks.
Risk: Model drift causing increased miss-rate. Mitigation: daily offline job that recomputes fingerprints and a decay factor for signatures older than 12h.
